recommendations: ABACUS: 144 push/PR workflows have no concurrency group; add `concurrency: {group: <workflow>-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true}` so superseded runs stop queueing.
ABACUS: 16 PR workflows run on every PR (no paths filter); add path filters to specialist ones (see the runner-fanout baseline).
CODEX: 124 push/PR workflows have no concurrency group; add `concurrency: {group: <workflow>-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true}` so superseded runs stop queueing.
CODEX: 30 PR workflows run on every PR (no paths filter); add path filters to specialist ones (see the runner-fanout baseline).
HUB: 119 push/PR workflows have no concurrency group; add `concurrency: {group: <workflow>-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true}` so superseded runs stop queueing.
HUB: 4 PR workflows run on every PR (no paths filter); add path filters to specialist ones (see the runner-fanout baseline).
3 cron minute(s) start more job slots than the 20 runners (worst 02:00 UTC: 49).
Staggering 12 cron(s) to other minutes cuts the peak start load from 49 to 23 job slots (see the stagger plan).
